banner.top: Note: this page is a demo. For real shortcut testing, go to any www. website (for example www.google.com) and try it in a normal text field.

hero.title:
Typed in the wrong
keyboard layout?
hero.sub: One shortcut detects and fixes layout mistakes in any text field on any website — instantly.
hero.shortcut: Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Alt</kbd> in any text field to fix

how.label: How It Works
how.title: Four phases, under a second
how.sub: Every Ctrl+Alt triggers a four-phase progressive scan with real-time visual feedback.

p1.p: A sweep animation plays across the input field — signals the scan is running.

p2.p: Each word is tested against both Arabic and English dictionaries to find layout mismatches.

p3.p: 🔴 Red box = will be converted. 🟠 Orange box = no dictionary match found.

p4.p: Words are replaced in the text. A toast previews all conversions. Undo button appears.

problem.label: The Problem
problem.title: We've all been there
problem.sub: You switch tabs, forget to change the keyboard layout, and start typing. By the time you notice, you've written a whole sentence in the wrong language.

c1.tag: Arabic intended → typed in English layout

c2.tag: English intended → typed in Arabic layout

c3.tag: Mixed sentence — only wrong words fixed

ctrlAlt.p: The main shortcut. Scans the entire focused field, highlights all words typed in the wrong layout, and converts them in one go. Only words that match a dictionary entry are converted — correct words in a mixed sentence are untouched.
ctrlAlt.label: Try it — click inside, press Ctrl+Alt
ctrlAlt.btn: ▶ Try it — Ctrl+Alt works here too

ctrlQ.h: Fix the word at the cursor
ctrlQ.p: Place your cursor inside a single wrong word and press Ctrl+Q. Only that one word is converted — the rest of the text is ignored. Useful when you spot one mistake mid-sentence without wanting to re-scan everything.
ctrlQ.label: Click inside a wrong word, then press Ctrl+Q
ctrlQ.btn: ▶ Try it — demo converts the whole field

ctrlShiftQ.p: Converts every word in the field regardless of dictionary results or language detection. Designed for users writing in languages beyond Arabic and English — Farsi, Urdu, or any other language that shares the Arabic script but is not yet in the dictionary. As the extension expands its language support, this shortcut remains the guaranteed fallback.
ctrlShiftQ.label: Try it — forces conversion of everything
ctrlShiftQ.btn: ▶ Try it — converts everything, no dictionary
ctrlShiftQ.hint: No dictionary check — every word remapped
ctrlShiftQ.explain1: only converts words it can verify in the dictionary — this protects intentional bilingual text
ctrlShiftQ.explain2: removes that filter entirely, making it the universal tool for any script-based layout swap.

ctrlZ.p: Every correction is saved in a per-session stack. Press Ctrl+Z immediately after any correction to restore the original text exactly as it was. Works for all three correction methods. Press multiple times to undo multiple corrections in reverse order.
ctrlZ.label: Step 1: Fix it → Step 2: Ctrl+Z to undo
ctrlZ.btn: ▶ Step 1: Fix it — then press Ctrl+Z to undo
ctrlZ.hint: Ctrl+Alt fixes it → Ctrl+Z restores the original

playground.label: Live Playground
playground.title: Every scenario, try it yourself
playground.sub: The extension must be installed and active. Click inside any field below, then press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>.
playground.noteTitle: Important: this page is a safe demo environment
playground.note1: Real auto-correction from the extension content script does not run on this page because it is loaded as chrome-extension://.... Chrome isolates extension pages for security, so content scripts are designed to run on regular websites instead.
playground.note2: The Fix it buttons below simulate the same behavior for learning purposes. To use the real shortcuts on live text fields, open any normal website and press Ctrl+Alt, Ctrl+Q, or Ctrl+Shift+Q. Go to any www. website (for example, www.google.com) and try it live there.

indicators.label: Visual Feedback
indicators.title: Everything you see, explained
indicators.sub: The extension communicates through four distinct visual elements. Here's what each one means.

red.p: Appears around words the extension has identified as wrong-layout and is about to convert. Flashes briefly before disappearing as the correction is applied.

orange.p: The word looks like a layout mistake but its converted form isn't in any dictionary. The extension won't guess — it flags it instead. Click the label above it to report the correct form.

purple.p: Shows a preview of all conversions: → word · → word. Tap "+N more" to expand if there are more than 5 words. Disappears on scroll or after 2.5 seconds.

green.p: Appears in the corner after every successful correction. Click it or press Ctrl+Z to instantly restore the original text. Disappears after a few seconds if not used.

report.label: Unknown Words
report.title: Flag, report, improve
report.sub: When a word can't be matched to any dictionary entry, the extension flags it instead of guessing. You can report the correct form to help improve the dictionary for everyone.

s1.p: The word stays in the text unchanged. An orange border surrounds it so you can see exactly which word was flagged.

s2.p: "⚠ not in dictionary — click to add 👆" appears above the box. Hover it to keep it visible. It auto-fades after 3 seconds.

s3.p: A panel appears anchored to the field. Type what the word should have been and submit — your correction goes directly into the dictionary improvement queue.

popup.label: Extension Popup
popup.title: Quick access from the toolbar
popup.sub: Click the extension icon in your Chrome toolbar to open the popup. It gives you a status overview and a direct feedback channel.

f1.p: Shows whether the extension is active on the current page.

f2.p: Opens a form to send suggestions, bug reports, or missing word requests directly to the developer.

f3.p: All four shortcuts listed at a glance — no need to remember them all.
